summary: All obligations remain disposed with no pending work and audit-unit capacity exhausted, and the run is near its time boundary, so this is a deliberately small continuation of the authorized source work. Submission is a feedback-only research product (no map version) that closes the two narrow transport items left open last step and re-checks the heartbeat classification. In-process queueing: NewInmemTransportWithTimeout builds the transport with a consumer channel of capacity 16 and a generated address when none is supplied (inmem_transport.go 53-65), so up to sixteen in-process RPCs can queue in a peer's channel before a sender blocks, on top of that sender's send timeout. Address provider: serverAddressProvider is taken once from the config at construction (net_transport.go 236) and serverAddressLock is only ever read in getProviderAddressOrFallback (389-398), so the library never mutates the provider after construction and the in-flight-dial race I had listed is withdrawn as not a library-side concern, since concurrency inside a caller-supplied provider is the caller's. Heartbeat classification: the leader's heartbeat goroutine emits an AppendEntriesRequest carrying only the RPC header, Term = s.currentTerm and the legacy leader address, with PrevLogEntry, PrevLogTerm, Entries and LeaderCommitIndex all zero (replication.go 388-395), which is exactly the shape the inbound transport classifies as a heartbeat, so the fast path does fire for real heartbeats as intended. Remaining list records that no transport item from the earlier lists is still open as a library responsibility, that caller-supplied StreamLayer wrappers including any TLS stay outside the library, that nothing in the transport reading was evaluated for defects so its correctness remains unmapped even though its behaviour is now largely described, and that the previously recorded open items are unchanged (installSnapshot watermark reachability, the compacted-leader variant, and execution corroboration of the two reading-based consequences). Preflight validation returns valid with no diagnostics.
